title: Getting ETIMEDOUT while running Telegraf bot in docker container with network mode host
body:
* Telegraf.js Version: Final version
* Node.js Version: v21
* Operating System: Ubuntu:latest

## Minimal Example Code Reproducing the Issue

```js
const { Telegraf } = require('telegraf')
const bot = new Telegraf('TELEGRAM_TOKEN')

bot.telegram.setMyCommands([
    {command: 'start', description: 'Starts the system'},
    {command: 'restart', description: 'Restarts the system'},
    {command: 'help', description: 'Show commands help'},
])
bot.start((ctx) => {
    console.log(new Date(), 'started:', ctx.from)
    return ctx.reply('Hello Boss')
})

bot.launch()
```

```Dockerfile
FROM ubuntu:latest

WORKDIR /usr/src/app

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install curl build-essential libpangocairo-1.0-0 libx11-xcb1 libxcomposite1 libxcursor1 libxdamage1 libxi6 libxtst6 libnss3 libcups2 libxss1 libxrandr2 libasound2 libatk1.0-0 libgtk-3-0 libxshmfence1 libgbm-dev openssl tesseract-ocr git libc++-dev chromium-browser -y

RUN curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_21.x | bash -
RUN apt-get install -y nodejs

COPY package.json ./package.json

RUN npm install
RUN npm install pm2 -g

COPY . .

CMD ["pm2-runtime", "--error", "./log/err.log", "--output", "./log/out.log" , "index.js"]

```
If I run docker container with network mode on host, with this command:

```
docker run --privileged -itd --mount type=bind,source=/ctb/log,target=/usr/src/app/log --network host --name ttelegraf hardc0der/ttelegraf:latest
```

I'm getting this error instantly:

```
FetchError: request to https://api.telegram.org/bot6411340281:[REDACTED]/setMyCommands failed, reason:
    at ClientRequest.<anonymous> (/usr/src/app/node_modules/node-fetch/lib/index.js:1501:11)
    at ClientRequest.emit (node:events:519:28)
    at TLSSocket.socketErrorListener (node:_http_client:492:9)
    at TLSSocket.emit (node:events:519:28)
    at emitErrorNT (node:internal/streams/destroy:169:8)
    at emitErrorCloseNT (node:internal/streams/destroy:128:3)
    at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:82:21) {
  type: 'system',
  errno: 'ETIMEDOUT',
  code: 'ETIMEDOUT'
}
```
I'm getting 200 response to my request when I logged in to container and make a CURL request to api.telegram.org

If I remove ```--network host``` from the running command, everything is running smoothly

What can be the reason to get this error while running in host mode network?

title: (WIP, DON'T MERGE) Fix typings in scenes/context.ts
Support Bot API 10.3 and modernize the v6 runtime
body:
## Summary

This updates the existing v6 proposal to Telegram Bot API **10.3**, and merges the latest official `v4` branch through `776b0f3`. The programming model remains Telegraf's middleware/Context/Telegram model, with current Bot API contracts and modern Node.js infrastructure.

### API and types

- Covers all **185 official Bot API methods**, checked against an independent snapshot of Telegram's 10.3 documentation as well as the installed declarations.
- Adds 10.x rich messages and drafts, live photos, guest queries, ephemeral messages, media in polls, join request queries, reaction management, subscriptions, and managed-bot additions.
- Updates Context accessors, formatting, upload handling, extra types, and `useNewReplies()` to carry the new fields without losing business/thread/reply context.
- Updates companion telegraf/types#14 to 10.3 using **upstream's unified `bot-api.ts` layout**, compatibility re-exports, and Bun/tsc/Oxlint/Oxfmt workflow. Its independent specification checks cover 185 methods and 399 object definitions, with positive/negative consumer type tests.
- Incorporates the inline rich-message upload restriction identified in @MKRhere's telegraf/types#17 and extends it to drafts. Telegram/Context compiler contracts reject upload objects for inline or possibly-inline edits and drafts, while preserving ordinary chat/ephemeral uploads and existing file IDs. Context narrowing and the remaining plain-string file-ID/URL limitation are documented in the release notes. This is type-level validation, not a new runtime payload validator.

### Integration with current upstream

- Includes the upstream multipart object-field serialization fix and its regressions.
- Retains upstream's async-generator multipart stream and removes `sandwich-stream`.
- Adds regression coverage for backpressure, large uploads, active/queued stream cleanup, attachment assembly failure, caller abort, timeout, and source stream errors.
- Requires Node >=22.20, with clean-install test/lint CI on Node 22.20, 24.12, and 26, following current upstream CI and AVA 8 requirements. A Node 20 validation exposed unsupported iterator APIs in the test toolchain; v6 no longer advertises Node 20 support. Updates compatible indirect dependencies to address available security fixes.
- Resolves the merge conflicts without rewriting the existing PR history.

### Runtime modernization

- Native `globalThis.fetch` is the default; Telegraf does not depend on `node-fetch`. Specialized networking is injectable through `telegram.fetch` for both API calls and URL attachments.
- Bot API transport and response-body failures cross a typed `TelegrafNetworkError` boundary. Diagnostics have sanitized causes and explicit error name/code/retryability; native errors are never mutated. API/HTTP failures remain `TelegramError`; both extend `TelegrafError`. Synchronous throws from injected fetch functions are handled too.
- Request timeouts cover response-body consumption, polling backoff is abortable, shutdown aborts are distinguished from unexpected aborts, and opt-in 409 retry remains available.
- Preserves previous follow-ups for launch callback timing, empty default sessions, scene typings, webhook rejection status codes, TypeScript 6, AVA 8, ESLint 9, and `p-timeout` 7.
- Updates README and v6 release notes for the current behavior and migration contract. This is an **unreleased candidate**, not a claim that official npm v6 is already available.

## Validation

- [Fork CI](https://github.com/Leask/telegraf/actions/runs/37213782922): all three jobs pass on Node **22.20 / 24.12 / 26** at `1b9fbba`. This is the fork's CI evidence, not a claim that upstream-required checks have been approved.
- [Companion types CI](https://github.com/Leask/types/actions/runs/37213409322): Node **20 / 22 / 24 / 26** all pass at `88aa916`.
- Clean `npm ci`, including an isolated-cache install without GitHub SSH credentials.
- `npm test`: **290 passing**, including compiler contracts and loopback HTTP tests. These are deterministic tests, not a claim that every operation was performed against a live Telegram bot.
- `npm run lint`: passes.
- `npm run build:docs`: passes, 0 errors; 86 TypeDoc reference/documentation warnings remain.
- `npm pack --dry-run`: passes; 168 intended package files, no tests, local configuration, or credentials included.
- `npm audit --omit=dev`: **0 vulnerabilities**.
- Full development audit: **4 high-severity reports remain in the `braces` -> `micromatch` -> `fast-glob` -> `globby` toolchain**. The published `braces` version is still 3.0.3 with no fixed release available at validation time. No forced downgrade or unverified override was used to hide these reports.
- `git diff --check`: passes.

## Temporary dependency and release gate

The 10.3 declarations are in https://github.com/telegraf/types/pull/14. This branch temporarily pins `@telegraf/types` to immutable HTTPS commit [`88aa916`](https://github.com/Leask/types/commit/88aa916e2ef6efe851da244f23d5532ef1526738). Imports stay unchanged. Installation requires Git but does not require GitHub SSH authentication.

This supersedes the previous `npm:@leask/types@9.6.0` alias because that published package does not contain the 10.3 declarations. **Replace the temporary pin with the official published 10.3 types package before an upstream release.** Neither an npm release nor an upstream merge is performed by this PR update.

## Future direction

Future Bot API updates should begin with Telegram's canonical definitions, update the independent specification fixture, and let structural type tests and runtime coverage checks identify missing methods and payload fields. Platform-standard Node.js APIs remain the default; advanced networking stays injectable instead of becoming a permanent bundled dependency.

The intent is to continue evolving with official upstream maintenance, not maintain a parallel architecture. This update preserves upstream's new type organization and stream implementation, and credits the reviewed 10.3 work ported from the hardened fork.

title: Slow code suggestions in Telegraf 4.16.X after update
body:
**Issue:** After updating Telegraf to version 4.16.X in VS Code, there is a noticeable slowdown in code suggestions. This issue was not present in version 4.15.3.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Update Telegraf to version 4.16.X in VS Code.
2. Observe the delay in code suggestions.
3. Downgrade to version 4.15.3.
4. Notice that code suggestions work normally with version 4.15.3.

https://github.com/telegraf/telegraf/assets/43033265/776a5323-d5ff-4d8c-abf4-e0d299cc3583


https://github.com/telegraf/telegraf/assets/43033265/51b4d75b-2099-4652-bcb3-74b539bc0b88


**Expected behavior:** Code suggestions should be as responsive as they were in version 4.15.3.

**Additional information:** Other users have reported similar issues after updating Telegraf. Some improvements were observed by disabling certain settings in tsserver LSP, but the problem persists.

**Versions:** 
- VS Code: 1.87.1 / 1.85 / 1.86
- Node js: 21.7.1 / 21.5.0
- Telegraf: 4.16.X (affected), 4.15.3 (not affected)
- Operating System: Windows

**Possible solution:** Investigate potential compatibility issues with extensions or configurations in tsserver LSP that may be causing the slowdown.

**Note:** Any help or insights to resolve this issue would be greatly appreciated. Thank you!

title: `createWebhook` always respond 404 with Koa
Runnable with CloudFlare Workers and other Edge Providers?
body:
I just got really excited when I noticed that v5 is removing `node-fetch` and moving to the native version.

I instantly tried installing it and using it for a deploy to Cloudflare Workers… sadly, I was out of luck.

I was greated with a bunch of erros about `node:path`, `node:util`, `node:stream/web` and maybe more being used which apparently are not available.

I also tried to activate `node_compat = true` in `wrangler` but that also did not help.

I hope telegraf can become fully edge compatible sometime. Or if I am missing something, please let me know.

Cheers
